question: Why were some claim payments loaded twice in June 2026?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: needs the LLM grader (Phase 3).

report.interpretation: You asked why some claim payments were loaded twice in June 2026. I checked claim_payments for rows that repeat on claim, payment date, amount and payee type, and looked at which load batch delivered each copy. I looked at all months, not only June.
report.answer: The premise is wrong. I found no duplicate payments in June 2026. All 159 duplicated payment rows are for March 2026, with payment dates from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13. Each one was loaded twice: once in its normal nightly batch, and again in a one-off batch named 'reload-2026-03-14', which was loaded outside the nightly process. The reload adds 159 extra rows worth about $893K. June 2026 payments each appear once, and every June row came from a normal nightly batch. The data doesn't say why the reload ran. It looks like a manual re-run or backfill that re-sent payments already loaded. Any paid-amount or incurred figure that includes March 2026 is overstated by about $893K until these rows are removed or excluded.
report.answer_sql: select load_batch, count(*) as row_count, sum(amount) as total_amount, min(payment_date) as first_payment, max(payment_date) as last_payment from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'nightly-%' group by load_batch

findings.claim: All 159 exact-duplicate payment rows are in March 2026, from the 'reload-2026-03-14' batch. None are in June 2026.
findings.evidence_sql: select strftime(payment_date,'%Y-%m') m, load_batch like 'reload%' as is_reload, count(*) from (select *, count(*) over (partition by claim_id,payment_date,amount,payee_type) c from claim_payments) where c>1 group by 1,2 order by 1

data_quality_issues.issue: Batch 'reload-2026-03-14' re-loaded 159 payments (dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13) that were already loaded in nightly batches.
data_quality_issues.impact: Paid amounts and incurred losses for March 2026 are overstated by about $893K, and payment counts by 159, unless these rows are excluded.

proposed_actions.title: Remove or flag duplicate rows from load batch reload-2026-03-14
proposed_actions.reason: 159 payments worth about $893K duplicate rows already loaded nightly, which inflates March 2026 paid and incurred figures. Data engineering should confirm why the reload ran and fix the data.

open_questions: Did you see a jump in June 2026 figures? If so, I can check that separately, because the duplicates aren't in June.
